items.passage: In presence of these vast spaces and all but unbounded outlook, the hours hurry by with singular ______. Minutes or miles are nothing; days and degrees seem best fitted for one’s thoughts. So it came sooner than I could have believed that the sun neared its setting, sinking into a warm, bright stratum of air. The light stretched from north to south, reflecting itself with an equal depth all along the east, until a perfect ring of soft, glowing rose edged the whole horizon. Over us the ever-dark heaven hung near and flat.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: slowness
heaviness
speed
silence
items.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 'the hours hurry by'는 시간이 빠르게 지나감을 직접 말한다. 이어지는 'sooner than I could have believed'도 해가 예상보다 일찍 졌다는 점에서 같은 의미를 뒷받침한다. 따라서 '빠름'을 뜻하는 C가 가장 적절하다. A와 B는 시간이 더디게 흐른다는 반대 의미이고, D는 시간의 흐름과 관련이 없다.

items.passage:
Here the wind blew freshly, and the great waves rolled and broke at Thistle’s feet, as he stood upon the shore, watching the billows dancing and sparkling in the sun.

“How shall I find the Spirits in this great sea, with none to help or guide me? Yet it is my last task, and for Lily-Bell’s sake I must not fear or falter now,” said Thistle. So he flew hither and thither over the sea, looking through the waves. Soon he saw, far below, the branches of the coral tree.

“They must be here,” thought he, and, folding his wings, he plunged into the deep, cold sea. But he saw only fearful monsters and dark shapes that gathered round him; and, trembling with ______, he struggled up again.

The great waves tossed him to and fro, and cast him bruised and faint upon the shore.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: delight
pride
boredom
fear
items.explanation: Thistle은 바닷속에서 'fearful monsters and dark shapes'만 보고 다시 올라온다. 앞서 그는 'I must not fear or falter now'라며 두려움을 이겨내려 했으므로 떨고 있는 이유는 두려움이다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 괴물에게 둘러싸인 상황과 떨리는 몸의 반응에 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: One can always see trouble who looks for it. I had never been across the plains and before the time for the train to start I walked to the front of the engine and looking along the track as it reached out across the prairie I saw trouble. What was it? Why, six miles ahead the track wasn't wide enough. Yes, I saw it. Then on six miles more the rails came together, with my destination nineteen hundred miles away. Soon the train moved and as we neared the difficulty, the track opened to welcome us. Not a pin was torn up nor a rail displaced. Again I looked ahead and a mountain was on the track, but before I had time to get off the mountain got off.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From alarm about obstacles ahead to wry amusement as they vanish
From cheerful confidence about the trip to deep regret over a missed destination
From quiet boredom with the prairie to angry frustration at the slow train
From calm curiosity about the engine to grim fear of a coming accident
items.explanation: 글은 화자가 앞길에서 'trouble'을 보았다며 걱정스러운 듯 시작한다. 그러나 기차가 다가가자 'the track opened to welcome us'라며 선로가 좁아 보인 것이 착시였음이 드러나고, 산조차 'got off'했다는 익살로 끝난다. 따라서 겉보기의 경계심에서 재치 있는 유머로 바뀌는 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 후회·분노·공포를 제시하지만 글 후반의 가벼운 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Is your world a small one, made unendurable by a thousand petty cares? Are the heart and soul of you cast down by bitter disappointment? Would you leave it all, if only for an hour, and come back with a new point of view? Then open the covers of a book.

With this gentle comrade, you may journey to the very end of the world and even to the beginning of civilisation. There is no land which you may not visit, from Arctic snows to the loftiest peaks of southern mountains. Gallant gentlemen will go with you and tell you how to appreciate what you see.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From cheerful praise of travel to stern warnings about the dangers of reading
From sympathy for readers' troubles to warm encouragement to read
From playful teasing of the reader to bitter complaints about civilisation
From formal description of distant lands to sorrowful memories of home
items.explanation: 글은 'small', 'petty cares', 'bitter disappointment' 같은 표현으로 독자의 괴로움을 묻는 공감 어린 질문으로 시작한다. 이후 'Then open the covers of a book' 다음부터는 책을 'gentle comrade'로 부르며 어디든 갈 수 있다는 따뜻한 권유로 바뀐다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 경고, C의 불평, D의 슬픈 회상은 지문에 나타나지 않는다.

items.passage:
Because your strife and labour have been vain,
Ye who have striven, shall I forego, forget
The far-off goal where to my feet were set
In the old days when life was first made plain?
Upward in April, who, meeting with the rain,
Did turn, the first shy mayflowers still are met?
I who have sought, yea, who am seeking yet,
What pain have I like unto your sore pain?
So let me go as one yearning, that braves,
With shipmen that have knowledge of the sea,
The wind disastrous and the ponderous waves
(Because his love dwells in some far countree),
Crying, "Not one of all your million graves
Is deep enough to keep my love from me!"
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From joyful celebration of spring to quiet grief over a lost friend
From angry blame of others to calm acceptance of a shared failure
From doubt about a distant goal to bold, defiant devotion
From hopeful planning of a voyage to fearful dread of the sea
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 다른 이들의 노력이 헛되었다고 해서 자신도 목표를 잊어야 하는지 'shall I forego, forget'처럼 의문을 품는다. 그러나 'So let me go' 이후로는 거친 바람과 파도를 무릅쓰는 뱃사람처럼 나아가겠다며 'Not one of all your million graves / Is deep enough'라고 외친다. 따라서 망설임에서 대담한 헌신으로 바뀌는 C가 정답이다. A, B, D는 각각 슬픔, 분노, 두려움을 제시해 시의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
ELSIE.

When I grow up I shall have eleven babies, because I have eleven favorite names, and I shall have them all at once, so they can have nice, happy times playing together, and there won't have to be any horrid older brother and sister, always getting the best of everything.

TERESA.

And I'll tell you what! I'll have eleven children too, to marry yours.

BOB.

No, I'll marry one of them.

ELSIE.

No, you must marry one of us.

BOB.

Which one?

ELSIE.

Well, I think it would be best for you to marry me and be father for my eleven children. I want them to have a father. I love my father.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From bitter quarreling among the children to a tearful apology from Bob
From serious talk about family duties to mocking laughter at the parents
From shy silence among the children to loud boasting about their toys
From playful fantasy about babies to sincere love for a parent
items.explanation: Elsie는 아이 열한 명을 한꺼번에 낳겠다는 엉뚱하고 장난스러운 상상으로 대화를 시작하고, 친구들도 결혼 상대를 정하는 놀이에 끼어든다. 그러다 마지막에 'I want them to have a father. I love my father.'라며 아버지에 대한 진심 어린 애정이 드러난다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 사과, B의 조롱, C의 자랑은 대화에 없다.

items.passage:
The flower clusters are nearly ready to bloom, but the buds are still green. The tall stem has lifted them up into the air and sunlight, and, although the air is still cold, they continue to grow.

Soon the green buds undergo a change. The topmost one on each flower cluster softens to a tender blue or pink.

The green buds grow lovely as they stand on their stems in the sun. Delicate tints steal over them, the green color fades away, and many colors take its place.

They open into charming flowers and give forth a delightful fragrance.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From plain notes on green buds to delighted praise of the blossoms
From eager hope for spring to disappointment at a late, cold spring
From scientific detachment about plants to anxious worry about frost
From gloomy description of winter to bored indifference toward flowers
items.explanation: 처음에는 꽃봉오리가 아직 초록색이고 줄기가 자란다는 사실을 담담하게 관찰한다. 이후 'grow lovely', 'Delicate tints', 'charming flowers', 'delightful fragrance' 같은 표현이 이어지며 감탄하는 어조로 바뀐다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B, C, D는 실망·걱정·무관심을 말하지만 글은 점점 기쁨을 드러낸다.

items.passage: Nevertheless the reporter, in summing up the achievement, is bound to declare that that other book has not been learned. Under this constitution of which I have been speaking, the American people have achieved much material success and great political power. As a people they have been happy and prosperous. Their freedom has been secured to them, and for a period of seventy-five years they have lived and prospered without subjection to any form of tyranny. This in itself is much, and should, I think, be held as a preparation for greater things to follow. Such, I think, should be our opinion, although the nation is at the present burdened by so heavy a load of troubles.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From joyful praise of the nation to angry rejection of its constitution
From criticism of an unlearned lesson to measured praise of gains
From hopeful predictions about the future to grim despair over present troubles
From humorous mockery of reporters to solemn respect for political leaders
items.explanation: 글은 'that other book has not been learned'라며 아직 배우지 못한 것이 있다는 비판적 판단으로 시작한다. 이어서 물질적 성공, 정치적 힘, 자유와 번영을 나열하며 'This in itself is much'라고 절제된 칭찬으로 바뀐다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 분노, C의 절망, D의 조롱은 지문의 어조와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Three honest generations of us have kept it clean and honorable, and our wives have done the same for us all down to you--all except my wife. I used to think that in marrying me you had placed me deeper in your debt than I could ever repay. Ever since the first time I saw you I loved you; and after that meeting I put my arms about no woman--arms that had been free enough before--until I put them around you. And since then the same. I have been an absolutely faithful husband to you. Do you understand what that means? I don't believe so. I preferred you to every other woman in the world.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From cheerful joking about his family to playful teasing of his wife
From cold anger at his wife to sudden forgiveness of her faults
From family pride to a pained insistence on his own loyalty
From calm business talk to nervous confusion about his past
items.explanation: 글은 'Three honest generations'로 가문의 명예를 자랑스럽게 이야기하며 시작한다. 그러나 'all except my wife' 이후에는 아내를 처음부터 사랑했고 'absolutely faithful husband'였다고 절박하고 개인적으로 호소한다. 'Do you understand what that means? I don't believe so.'에는 상처받은 감정이 드러나므로 C가 정답이다. A, B, D의 장난, 용서, 혼란은 지문에서 찾을 수 없다.

items.passage:
Suddenly the roof was lifted and whirled down the swollen arroyo into the broad river. Floating logs struck against it, and as they tore along under the bridge they struck against the buttress with terrific force. Onward they were whirled; they could see the lights in the houses of the village and could hear the voices of men and women along the bluffs or in the trees where they had sought shelter.

The rain ceased falling, but the wind did not go down, rolling the waves over their raft. Once they lodged for a moment against a great oak where Crescimir strove in vain to make fast.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It explains why a flood happened and then describes how the village was rebuilt
It describes a calm evening and then recalls an earlier storm in the village
It introduces Crescimir's past and then explains why he fears the river
It traces the roof's rush downstream and then a failed try to stop it
items.explanation: 글은 지붕이 들려 강으로 휩쓸려 가고 통나무에 부딪히며 마을을 지나가는 과정을 순서대로 묘사한다. 이어서 비는 그쳤지만 바람이 계속되고, 큰 참나무에 잠시 걸렸을 때 Crescimir가 'strove in vain to make fast'했다는 실패한 시도로 끝난다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 재건, B의 회상, C의 인물 과거는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: I threw out my arms, expecting to catch the living body of some person; but not so--I caught nothing. As I turned round I felt the same touch on my right cheek. It might have been imagination, but I thought I again heard Lottie calling my name. The truth is, I was so much overcome with excitement that I scarcely knew what was going on around me. Harry was out but a few moments, returning accompanied by the fireman, who immediately lighted the lamp. We procured a lantern and began to search for the mysterious passenger. We carefully examined every seat, looking under each bench, but could find nobody. We went out and examined the rear platform, thinking that probably some one might be stealing a ride, but nothing of the sort was to be seen.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It moves from a strange touch to a careful search that finds no one
It moves from a cheerful journey with Harry to an argument with the fireman
It moves from a search of the train to a calm explanation of the noise
It moves from Lottie's arrival to the narrator's decision to leave the car
items.explanation: 화자는 먼저 뺨에 닿는 이상한 감촉과 Lottie가 부르는 듯한 소리를 경험한다. 이후 Harry와 소방수가 등불을 켜고 좌석 밑과 뒤쪽 승강장까지 살피지만 'could find nobody'라고 한다. 따라서 이상한 경험에서 아무도 찾지 못한 수색으로 이어지는 A가 정답이다. B의 말다툼, C의 설명, D의 Lottie 도착은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: In most things we have given up the theory. It was soonest given up as regards food, because the evidence against it was there plainest and most overwhelming, in the severe suffering inflicted on some people by things "disagreeing with them," as it was called, which others relished and profited by. It has only been surrendered with regard to children and youths, however, after a hard struggle. The idea of a young person being entitled to special treatment of any kind--that is, having in any respect a marked individuality--remains to this day odious to a great many of our theologians and teachers. It is, however, rapidly making its way, and has already obtained a secure footing in some of the colleges.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It praises a theory and then lists the colleges that first adopted it
It notes where a theory was dropped, then its slow retreat in schools
It describes a personal illness and then blames teachers for causing it
It defends theologians and then predicts that their views will spread
items.explanation: 글은 먼저 사람마다 다르게 대하지 않는다는 이론이 음식에서는 가장 빨리 포기되었다고 설명한다. 이어서 아이와 청년에 대해서는 'after a hard struggle'로 늦게 포기되었고, 지금도 일부 신학자와 교사는 거부하지만 'rapidly making its way'라고 한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 지문의 흐름이나 입장과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Against this preference shown the sketch it may be urged that to appreciate such suggestions presupposes as much art in the public as in the painter. But the ability to appreciate a thing when expressed is but half that necessary to express it. Some understanding must exist in the observer for any work to be intelligible. It is only a question of degree. The greater the art-sense in the person addressed, the more had better be left to it. Now in Japan the public is singularly artistic. In fact, the artistic appreciation of the masses there is something astonishing to us, accustomed to our immense intellectual differences between man and man. Sketches are thus peculiarly fitting to such a land.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It tells a story about a painter and then describes his travels in Japan
It praises detailed paintings and then criticizes the Japanese public
It answers an objection to sketches and then applies it to Japan
It compares several artists and then ranks their finished works
items.explanation: 글은 스케치를 선호하는 것에 대해 대중에게도 화가만큼의 예술 감각이 필요하다는 반론을 제시한다. 이어 감상하는 능력은 표현하는 능력의 절반이면 된다고 답하고, 일본 대중의 예술 감각이 뛰어나므로 'Sketches are thus peculiarly fitting'이라고 결론짓는다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 여행, B의 비판, D의 순위는 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
One can see the almost devilish satisfaction he took in it by his giving it his name.

He was always proud of telling how he entered Philadelphia for the first time, with nothing in the world but two shillings in his pocket and four rolls of bread under his arm. __But really, when you come to examine it critically, it was nothing.__ Anybody could have done it.

To the subject of this memoir belongs the honor of recommending the army to go back to bows and arrows in place of bayonets and muskets. He observed, with his customary force, that the bayonet was very well under some circumstances, but that he doubted whether it could be used with accuracy at a long range.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers proof that the subject was a skilled military planner
It explains why the subject chose to move to Philadelphia
It describes the subject's poverty in serious, sympathetic detail
It mocks a famous story by dismissing it as no achievement at all
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 바로 앞에서 그는 두 실링과 빵 네 개만 들고 필라델피아에 왔다는 이야기를 자랑스럽게 한다. 밑줄 문장과 이어지는 'Anybody could have done it'은 그 유명한 일화를 별것 아닌 것으로 깎아내리는 풍자다. 활과 화살로 돌아가자는 제안을 다루는 마지막 단락도 같은 조롱조이므로 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 글의 풍자적 어조를 놓쳤다.

items.passage:
Perhaps a promise to another or some vow! But I swore to myself that, whatever the obstacle might be, I would remove it. The only matter for present disposition was to get her consent to my doing so.

She would soon return, composed and smiling, with no sign of wishing to elude me. For the life of me, I could not long refrain from the subject that had before so strangely put her to flight.

Sometimes when I talked in the strain of love, joy and pain would succeed each other on her face, sometimes they would seem to be present at the same moment. __From the look of complete abandonment to happiness that sometimes, though never for long, shone on her features, I felt that she loved me, and that eventually her love would gain the victory.__
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives the narrator's reason for thinking her love will win out
It reveals that the narrator has given up hope of winning her consent
It explains the promise or vow that keeps her from accepting him
It describes her decision to leave rather than discuss the subject
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 어떤 장애물이든 제거하겠다고 다짐하지만 그녀는 사랑 이야기가 나오면 자리를 피했다. 밑줄 문장은 그녀의 얼굴에 잠시 떠오르는 행복의 표정을 근거로 그녀가 자신을 사랑하며 결국 그 사랑이 이길 것이라는 믿음을 밝힌다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 화자의 희망과 반대이고, C의 약속 내용과 D의 떠나는 결정은 지문에 나오지 않는다.

items.passage:
Nothing so compliments a man as for a woman to believe in him--nothing so pleases a woman as for a man to place confidence in her.

__Obey? God help me! Yes, if I loved a woman, my whole heart's desire would be to obey her slightest wish.__ And how could I love her unless I had perfect confidence that she would only aspire to what was beautiful, true and right? And to enable her to realize this ideal, her wish would be to me a sacred command; and her attitude of mind toward me I know would be the same. And the only rivalry between us would be as to who could love the most; and the desire to obey would be the one controlling impulse of our lives.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It rejects the idea that love requires any trust between partners
It turns a question about obedience into a vow of devotion
It describes a quarrel the writer once had with a woman he loved
It warns readers that obedience in marriage leads to rivalry
items.explanation: 첫 문장은 믿음과 신뢰가 서로를 기쁘게 한다는 일반적 생각을 제시한다. 밑줄 문장은 'Obey?'라는 물음을 던진 뒤 사랑한다면 그녀의 작은 바람에도 따르겠다는 헌신으로 답한다. 이후 문장들은 서로 순종하려는 마음이 삶을 이끈다고 이 생각을 발전시키므로 B가 정답이다. A, C, D는 지문의 주장과 반대이거나 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
__Great caution, however, was necessary to prevent any possible mishap.__ First, the largest and strongest mule in the drove was relieved of his burden and forced to cross the river alone. He examined it very suspiciously and at first hesitated about entering the water. But he was so belabored with sticks and clubs that the poor beast had no alternative. After he had started towards the other side the peons all kept up such an unearthly yell that he was afraid to venture back. After a terrific struggle he succeeded in reaching the opposite bank.

The current was evidently still too strong to warrant another experiment of this kind. So we waited about a half an hour, when a second mule--a smaller one--was driven into the water.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the mule's fear after it reached the opposite bank
It explains why the peons yelled at the animals from the shore
It introduces the careful river test that follows
It concludes that the current was too strong to cross at all
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 사고를 막기 위해 큰 주의가 필요했다고 말한다. 이후 가장 크고 강한 노새를 먼저 짐 없이 건너보게 하고, 물살이 여전히 세서 반 시간을 기다린 뒤 작은 노새를 보낸다는 조심스러운 절차가 이어진다. 따라서 뒤이어 나오는 신중한 시험 방법을 소개하는 C가 정답이다. A, B는 세부 사항일 뿐이고, D는 결국 건너기를 계속했다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Washington Flagg was gone, but his shadow was to linger for a while longer on our household. It was difficult to realize that the weight which had oppressed us had been removed. We were scarcely conscious of how heavy it had been until it was lifted. I was now and then forced to make an effort not to expect the colonel to dinner.

A month or two after his disappearance an incident occurred which brought him back very vividly and in a somewhat sinister shape to our imaginations. Quite late one night there was a sharp ring at the door. Mary having gone to bed, I answered the bell.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Washington Flagg?
options: Relief at his absence mixed with a lingering unease
Deep sorrow over his departure and eagerness for his quick return
Amused fondness for his habits and regret at having sent him away
Complete indifference to him and his effect on the household
items.explanation: 화자는 그가 떠나 'the weight which had oppressed us'가 사라졌다고 하며 안도감을 드러낸다. 그러나 'his shadow was to linger'와 그가 'in a somewhat sinister shape'로 다시 떠올랐다는 표현에서 여전한 불안이 보인다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 C는 그를 그리워하는 태도로 지문과 반대이고, D는 그의 영향을 계속 의식한다는 점과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: I went mad, mad, I really did. I made up my mind to have a house I could live in comfortably, and I was generous enough to let my husband have something he liked too. Do you know, before he married me, fond as he was of his pictures and china and things, it had never occurred to him to build a place to put them in? But I changed all that. I practically rebuilt the house, as you see; let in a little light and air into the musty corners; let him have a gallery which has become the joy of his heart.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the changes she made to the house?
options: She regrets them because they ruined her husband's collection
She is proud of them and sees them as a gift to him
She is unsure of them and worries that guests will disapprove
She is bored by them and wishes she had left the house alone
items.explanation: 화자는 집을 거의 다시 지었다며 'But I changed all that'이라고 자신 있게 말한다. 또 남편에게 갤러리를 마련해 주어 'the joy of his heart'가 되었다고 하며 'generous enough'라고 스스로를 칭찬한다. 따라서 자랑스러워하며 남편을 위한 선물로 여기는 B가 정답이다. A, C, D의 후회, 불안, 지루함은 지문에서 찾을 수 없다.

items.passage:
Ye dwell beside our paths and homes,
Our paths of sin, our homes of sorrow,
And guilty man, where'er he roams,
Your innocent mirth may borrow.
The birds of air before us fleet,
They cannot brook our shame to meet--
But we may taste your solace sweet,
And come again to-morrow.

Ye fearless in your nests abide--
Nor may we scorn, too proudly wise,
Your silent lessons undescried
By all but lowly eyes;
For ye could draw th' admiring gaze
Of Him who worlds and hearts surveys:
Your order wild, your fragrant maze,
He taught us how to prize.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the flowers addressed in the poem?
options: Fearful suspicion of their wild and tangled growth
Mild annoyance that they distract people from prayer
Humble admiration for their comfort and lessons
Proud scorn for their silent and lowly existence
items.explanation: 화자는 꽃들이 죄와 슬픔의 길가에 있으면서 'innocent mirth'와 'solace sweet'를 준다고 말한다. 또 'Nor may we scorn, too proudly wise'라며 꽃의 'silent lessons'를 겸손한 눈만이 알아본다고 하고, 신도 그것을 소중히 여기라 가르쳤다고 한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 부정적 태도이고, D는 화자가 직접 부정한 오만한 경멸이다.
